## 214. F3's CONSUMER — the per-valkrets voter-group view, and the campaign's electorate is the roll (2026-09-02)

**What §213's marginals now feed.** Three things, one commit:

1. **`SwedishValkretsPopulation2024`** (`Assets/Scripts/Elections/Generated/`), a generated catalog from `valkrets_population_by_age_2024.csv` and `valkrets_municipalities_2024.csv` by `ValkretsPopulationCatalogGenerator` — `Names[29]` in the statute's order and Valmyndigheten's form (parenthetical stripped, " valkrets" stripped, trailing " läns" → " län", so every name joins `SwedishValkretsReturns2022.Names`), `Bands[29][21]`, `Total[29]`, and both sources' SHA-256 as `SourceDigest`/`NamesDigest`. `GeneratedCatalogCheck.CheckValkretsPopulation` re-derives the digests, asserts 29 rows whose bands sum to their totals and to the national **10 587 710**, and that 0 names are unjoined.
2. **`CohortVoterGroups.ForValkrets(v)`** / `ValkretsPyramid(v)` / `ValkretsIndex(name)` — the same 13-group view C-D1 built nationally, over each valkrets's own 2024 pyramid. `VoterGroupViewDiagnostic` now sweeps all 29 after the national table: every view sums to 1 and every name joins; **CLEAN**.
3. **`RegionAudience.Eligible`** — the campaign's regions carry the mobilisable electorate as a field distinct from the audience; C-N2's turnout term (`CampaignAi`) and the ground-game ledger (`CampaignRun`) read it. `LiveCampaignSetup.SwedenRegions` fills it from **Valmyndigheten's 2022 roll** (`SwedishValkretsReturns2022.Eligible`), not from the new file — see the finding.

**The finding, measured before it was decided.** The diagnostic prints each valkrets's 18+ RESIDENTS (2024, from the marginals) beside the 2022 ROLL. The ratio is never 1: **1.03 (Gotland) to 1.09 in the county valkretsar, 1.11–1.16 in Stockholms kommun (1.109), Uppsala (1.111), Göteborg (1.137), Stockholms län (1.143) and Malmö (1.155)** — non-citizen adult residents plus two years' growth, largest exactly where the immigrant population is. A first draft asserted the two within 10 % and failed the four metropolitan valkretsar; the assertion was wrong, not the data, because the file counts residents and a campaign mobilises voters. So the electorate is the roll, the marginals contribute the AGE STRUCTURE of each valkrets's voters, and the diagnostic prints the ratio without asserting an identity. An SCB citizenship cut is the fetch that would let the 2024 file carry the electorate itself (billed in the README).

**The second finding: the view has no game-path reader, and the ratchets said so.** With the electorate taken from the roll, nothing on the game path names `CohortVoterGroups` — it never did (C-D1 left it Editor-consumed), and the campaign has no age-group mechanic for it to feed. I had lowered `UnwiredSubsystemCheck`'s two ceilings 3 → 2 on the belief that the consumer was wired; the bar measured 3 UNWIRED and 3 UNREACHABLE (`CohortVoterGroups`, `Rosatellum`, `TacticalVoting`'s entry point / `ElectoralCollege`) and failed. The ceilings are back at the committed **3 / 3** — not raised, restored from an uncommitted mistake — with the reason in their comments. The view's honest consumer is the per-group design (targeting by age group), which waits on per-group loyalty (Elias's, ITANES). To make that wait informed, the diagnostic prints one more measurement per valkrets: its turnout as its 2024 age mix weights SCB's 2014 band rates, beside its ACTUAL 2022 turnout (`Cast / Eligible`). **The age mix predicts a spread of 0.4 points (85.4–85.8) across the 29; the actual 2022 spread is 10.3 points (Malmö 77.2, Göteborg 80.7, Stockholms län 82.5 … Västra Götalands västra 87.6).** Age structure carries almost none of Sweden's regional turnout variation; the low-turnout valkretsar are the high resident-to-roll ones, which points at the citizenship/immigration composition, not the pyramid. That is the per-group design's first fact: a per-valkrets AGE view would not improve the campaign's regional turnout, and the actual per-valkrets turnout (`Cast / Eligible`, already sourced) is the better public fact if the campaign ever wants one.

**The digest moved, and the family is explained.** C-N2 previously took each region's mobilisation headroom off its AUDIENCE (the valid vote); it now takes it off the ELIGIBLE roll, larger in every valkrets (2022 turnout 84.2 %), so the ground game's headroom per region grew and the AI's door-knocking scores shifted. Campaign digest `7315ebd8d034cfd1` → **`854ed57927e38bc2`** — and it is the same digest whether `Eligible` is the roll or the 18+ resident count, so the base's LEVEL moved decisions and its regional pattern did not. Personalities hold (`CampaignAiHarness` 2a-ii L1 0.405, chaotic 0.687, grassroots 1.217 / 0.973); reactivity, strategy and attribution harnesses green; `SaveLoadRoundTripDiagnostic` USA and Sweden 8-turn continuations identical.

**Still billed in F3:** per-group loyalty (Elias's, ITANES), the Italy re-run behind it, the per-group targeting design that would put the view on the game path, and the education/income marginals (SCB UF0506, HE0110).

## 215. F3's THIRD CLAUSE — the income and education marginals per valkrets, and a source that does not add up (2026-09-02)

**What landed.** C-D1's remaining two marginals, fetched from SCB's PxWeb API by POST and mapped to the 29 valkretsar through §213's statute mapping (`ElectionsData/sweden/`, `Tools/build_valkrets_marginals.sh`, the README's new section):

- **Income** — `HE0110A/SamForvInk1`, persons by *sammanräknad förvärvsinkomst* class, all 290 municipalities × 15 age bands × 26 classes, 2024 → `valkrets_income_by_age_class_2024.csv` (29 × 15 rows).
- **Education** — `UF0506B/UtbBefRegionR`, population 16–95+ by SUN level, single year and sex, all 290 municipalities, 2024, fetched in four parts under the API's 150 000-cell limit → `valkrets_education_by_age_2024.csv` (29 × 17 five-year bands × 8 levels).

**Two measured properties of the sources, recorded rather than smoothed.**

1. **The income table suppresses 16 888 of 125 280 cells** (`..`, under 3 persons — the smallest published value is 3), all in age × class cells; every band's TOT is published. So each valkrets-band row carries `unpublished` = TOT − Σ published classes: net **27 082 of 8 561 924 persons (0.32 %)**. A consumer takes the class shares as published and names the residual; it does not spread it.
2. **The income table is not additive to the person.** Its 16+ TOT over municipalities is 8 561 886 against Riket's own 8 561 903; its band TOTs sum to 8 561 924; per municipality the band TOTs differ from the 16+ TOT in 269 of 290 cases by −14..+14; and in 89 of 435 valkrets-band rows the published classes EXCEED the band total (worst −48). That is SCB's disclosure control, not the mapping — the education table, mapped through the identical file, reconciles to Riket **to the person, per level** (8 682 407, eight levels exact against a separately fetched Riket row). The premise that a publisher's table is additive was measured before anything was built on it, and for this one it is false by tens of persons per municipality.

**Nothing built, by the ratchet's rule.** These are residents, not the electorate (the age marginal's own caveat, §214); their job is the voter-group view's non-demographic axis, which is the per-group design that waits on per-group loyalty (Elias's). A catalog with no game-path reader would count against `UnwiredSubsystemCheck`'s ceilings, which §214 measured at their limit — so the data lands as a discharged bill, the way the tax and participation sources did. **All three of C-D1's marginals are discharged.**

It needs OCR, which is not a tool here. Italy alone stays billed, with the route that would work named.

## 217. P2-0.1 — THE DEFICIT BASIS BUG: measured, and it was the one-time settlements, not a SEK line (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 0): *"Measure first: which figure on Statistics › Domestic mixes a national-unit (SEK) line with a USD total. The likeliest seam is the budget decomposition's sourced lines against the USD seed."*

**The measurement is `DomesticMoneyBasisDiagnostic`** (Editor, in `CheckSuite.Simulation`), and its first run was red — that run is the record (`PoliSim-captures/logs/p2_0_1_measure.log`). It traces every money figure the Domestic sheet prints to its basis, per country:

1. **The seed.** GDP, the debt stock, the Debt-to-GDP identity, GDP per capita's identity, and every seeded spending line as a share of GDP. **All six countries clean.** The sourced decompositions (Sweden's utgiftsområden, the four R-K7 budgets) are share weights over the game's own total by construction, and the diagnostic proves it by measurement: no seeded line above its ceiling, no portfolio above its ceiling. ⚠ **The SEK hypothesis is measured false** — there is no national-unit line on the sheet.
2. **After two closed years.** The report's revenue, spending and balance as shares of GDP, the sheet's deficit sign convention against the report's balance over the same GDP. **All six clean.** (The cumulative accumulator is printed beside the year's balance — P2-0.4's fact, asserted there, not here.)
3. **The one-time settlements — where the basis actually broke.** Every option in the cabinet decision pool and the foreign-policy meeting pool carries a `BudgetImpact` authored in the game's billions when the USA was the only playable country, and `CabinetSystem.ApplyDecisionOption` / `ForeignPolicySystem.ApplyMeetingOption` applied it **unscaled to whichever country decided**. The run before the fix, verbatim:

```
  USA      largest as applied  +220.0 =  0.75% of GDP (unscaled it was  +220.0 =   0.75% of GDP)  <- cabinet: Loophole Closure Package / Push it through
  Sweden   largest as applied  +220.0 = 35.14% of GDP (unscaled it was  +220.0 =  35.14% of GDP)  <- cabinet: Loophole Closure Package / Push it through
  Germany  largest as applied  +220.0 =  4.60% of GDP
  France   largest as applied  +220.0 =  6.68% of GDP
  Italy    largest as applied  +220.0 =  9.65% of GDP
  Poland   largest as applied  +220.0 = 26.36% of GDP
```

   One "Push it through" on a Swedish Finance minister's decision moved Sweden's books by a third of its GDP. That is a deficit figure with two bases on one screen — the year's flows on Sweden's scale and a settlement on the USA's — and it is what a player sees as the Budget Balance headline after a cabinet decision. The infrastructure, welfare and SWF flows are all shares of GDP and were never affected; only the two authored pools were.

**The fix, at the seam.** `AuthoredImpactScale` (Simulation) states the authored basis once — the USA seed's GDP, read off `WorldFactory.UsaSeedGdp`, which is now the single statement of that seed and is used in the USA's own constructor call — and converts: an authored settlement lands as **the same share of the deciding country's current GDP**. Both apply sites route through it; the two option types' `BudgetImpact` fields document the basis. Nothing at the display moved. The run after the fix (`p2_0_1_after2.log`):

```
  USA      largest as applied  +221.8 =  0.76% of GDP (unscaled it was  +220.0 =   0.75% of GDP)
  Sweden   largest as applied    +4.8 =  0.76% of GDP (unscaled it was  +220.0 =  35.14% of GDP)
  Germany  largest as applied   +36.2 =  0.76% of GDP (unscaled it was  +220.0 =   4.60% of GDP)
  France   largest as applied   +25.0 =  0.76% of GDP (unscaled it was  +220.0 =   6.68% of GDP)
  Italy    largest as applied   +17.3 =  0.76% of GDP (unscaled it was  +220.0 =   9.65% of GDP)
  Poland   largest as applied    +6.3 =  0.76% of GDP (unscaled it was  +220.0 =  26.36% of GDP)
```

**The correction per country, stated:** the USA at seed is byte-identical (the factor is exactly one; asserted on a fresh seed world — the diagnostic's own first version asked it of a USA that had closed two years and reported growth as a defect, which is the ordering error the comment there now names); after the seed the USA's settlements scale with its GDP, which is the honest reading of a settlement as a share of the economy that pays it. Sweden's settlements shrink to roughly a forty-sixth of what they were, Poland's to a thirty-fifth, Italy's to a thirteenth, France's to a ninth, Germany's to a sixth — each now the same share of its own GDP as the authored figure is of the USA seed's. **Class: SAFE for the trajectory bar** — neither pool is reached by `TrajectoryBaselineDump` (cabinet decisions roll only for appointed ministers and are resolved only by the controller; meetings roll only in `AdvanceCountryDayTick`), so the no-policy trajectories cannot move; the change reaches play, and only play.

**The harness that asserts one basis** is the same diagnostic, now green and armed: the identities, the seeded shares, the closed-year shares, and every pooled settlement under its ceiling on every country. Its ceilings are directions (S-37): growth above any of them fails; none is a target.

**What was not done.** The four figures on the sheet the sheet itself derives — the deficit rows named by sign, GDP per capita, the impact ledger's money lines — were traced and not touched: each reads one state field in the seed's unit. The Budget Balance headline still shows the cumulative accumulator, which is P2-0.4's row, next.

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` 10 of 10 (the diagnostic among them) and `RunAllBatch` 25 of 25 clean on the committed tree (`bar23_p2_0_1_*.log`).

## 218. P2-0.2 — THE LEGACY ELECTION RESULT: it fired on every election, it drew OVER election night, and it is retired (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 0): *"Establish whether `ElectionSystem`'s approval-threshold 'Re-Elected' path still fires now that C-R4b gives the player a party. If it does, retire it — the last D0 clause."*

**Established: it fired, and worse than the row feared.** `GameController.CheckElection` ran `ElectionSystem.RunElection` on every election turn and stored an `ElectionResult`; `OnGUI` then drew `DrawElectionResultsScreen` — "RE-ELECTED" or "ELECTION LOST" over an approval bar with the 35-point threshold marked — while `_pendingElectionResult` was non-null. D-5 (a) had narrowed the *verdict* to the four countries without a live vote model, but the *screen* was unconditional. And it sat on top of the real thing: election night (board 1h) is a `ScreenSpaceOverlay` Canvas built by `ShowElectionNight` in the same call, and IMGUI draws above every Canvas (the render-order finding S-20 recorded for the capture harness), so **on every election ever played the player saw the approval reveal, pressed Continue, and the desk painted straight back over the night, which was then destroyed unseen at the next turn.** Election night, wired at F1 step 4 and recorded as reachable, had never been visible in play. The reveal was the last clause of the pre-item-10 politics — D0's map of what item 10 replaces named `PartyArchetype`, `TotalSeats = 200` and `ElectionSystem`'s approval threshold, and this was the third.

**Retired, at every site:**

- `ElectionSystem` keeps only the calendar (`ElectionCycle`, `IsElectionTurn`); `ElectionResult`, `LosingThreshold` and `RunElection` are deleted, and the class comment says what replaced them.
- `GameController`: the pending result, its OnGUI gate, the reveal screen and `DismissElectionResult` are gone. `CheckElection` now runs the country's vote, resolves the office test at once (`ResolveElectionVerdict`, C-R4's rule as D-5 (a) ruled it: in cabinet continues, out of cabinet ends the game, no government formed continues and says so), holds the verdict's sentence, and shows election night **as a takeover in the canvas seam** — a new `CanvasScreenKind.ElectionNight` with the same cover-in / reveal / cover-out the signing document uses. The clock holds on it (the day loop's gates name `_electionNight`), IMGUI suppresses itself under it, and **CONTINUE on the board's foot is its only exit**; the verdict lands after the cover-out, on the desk (`ApplyElectionVerdict`), never under a screen the player is still reading. A country whose vote model returns NotImplemented holds no election and reaches no verdict — the record's `NotHeldReason` says why — and shows nothing rather than something false. ⚠ **That makes those four countries unlosable at an election until their vote model lands**, which is the consequence D-5 (a) declined and Elias's row now rules: one election path, or none.
- `ElectionNightScreen` gains the foot: the verdict line (when a player is on the ballot) and the brass CONTINUE (the signing screen's own button pattern), plus `Dismiss` / `SetVisible` / `Destroy` for the seam.
- The save carries the verdict (`PendingElectionVerdict`, `PendingElectionVerdictEndsGame`) instead of an `ElectionResult`; a load with one pending lands it at once, because the night it was shown on is in-process state and cannot be rebuilt — stated in the load path rather than lost.
- `UiScreenshotDriver`'s state pass no longer forces approval to film a WIN and a LOSS reveal; it films `88n_election_night_takeover` for a country with a live vote model, dismisses through the controller's own `DismissElectionNight`, and films what follows (`88b_game_over` or `88c_after_election_night`). A country without a night says so in the log rather than filming the desk under the night's name.
- `CLAUDE.md`'s Elections bullet carries the dated correction; `ScenarioLibrary`'s comment no longer cites the threshold.

**The harness that proves the old path unreachable** is a clause added to `OfficeTestDiagnostic` (simulation group, no new check — R-N5): reflection asks `ElectionSystem` for `LosingThreshold`, `RunElection` and the `ElectionResult` type, and a comment-stripped scan of every file under `Assets/Scripts` asks for the identifiers. A deleted path's only proof is absence, and this is it, armed.



**The film, and what it found on the way.** The state pass (`-shotstates`, Sweden, 1280 — `p2night1280.log`) could not film the night: it reported no board after `CheckElection`, and nothing in the controller said why, because every early exit of `ShowElectionNight` was silent. That silence is the class S-20 named, so each exit now logs its reason (`ELECTION: no election night for … - …`), the not-held branch logs the record's reason, and a held election logs its method and whether a campaign result was counted. The same pass exposed the harness trap recorded in the environment memory: a **docked Game View ignores the position assignment** `ResizeGameView` relies on, so the whole pass filmed at the dock's size with every frame reporting a HEIGHT MISMATCH — the guard working. `UiScreenshotCapture.ResizeGameView` now closes a docked view that ignored the size and re-creates it floating, and logs which happened. The pass also reported three trace-panel misnames on Sweden's scenario captures (`94b`, `95b`, `95d`: *"the trace panel is NOT open on Approval / Debt-to-GDP"*); those captures assume the USA's trace state and are a finding for the state pass's own owner, not touched here.

The instrument that films the night is the driver's new **`-shotinterrupts`** mode: it plays ONE country's game through the controller-shaped day path (the campaign begins, runs and is counted exactly as play makes it), enters the election through the controller's own `CheckElection`, and proves the takeover by watching the date with the clock set to VeryFast — a date that does not move is a held clock, not a slow frame; a missing night is a failure, not a skipped frame. **Sweden, seed 777, both widths** (`p2int1280_*.png`, `p2int2560_*.png`; logs `p2int1280.log`, `p2int2560.log`): `ELECTION: held for Sweden at turn 4 by SwedenTwoTier (a campaign result exists)` — the campaign's shares counted through the tactical layer — then `e7c_election_night_takeover` with the count, the verdict on the foot (*out of office: the chamber formed a M+KD+L government with S in opposition*) and CONTINUE; `SHOT: the clock is HELD on election night`; then `e7d_after_election_night_gameover`, the desk under the GAME OVER stamp carrying the same sentence. ⚠ Two things the frames show that are NOT this row's: the hold banner over the night names the foreign-policy meeting waiting behind it rather than the night itself (P2-0.3's "the banner names it" covers election night too), and the strip's BUDGET BALANCE is the cumulative accumulator (P2-0.4).

**Bar:** the first run (`bar24_p2_0_2_*.log`) went red on `CommentImmunityCheck` - the office diagnostic now reads source and was enrolled in neither of the immunity census's lists, which is that check doing its job; enrolled in the must-strip list (it routes through the stripper), both groups clean on the committed tree (`bar24b_p2_0_2_*.log`).

## 219. P2-0.3 — THE CAMPAIGN ANNOUNCES ITSELF: the opening is an interrupt, election night names itself on the banner (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 0): *"Campaign start is an interrupt: the clock HELDs, the banner names it, and HQ opens (the Fed-chair pause is the template). Election night is entered the same way — never a screen the player can miss."*

**Before.** The player's campaign began inside the sim's own day (`SimulationManager.AdvanceCampaign`, C-R4b step 3) with a log line and nothing else: the rail grew a CAMPAIGN cell and the clock ran on. A player watching the desk at 2× passed the eight weeks without opening HQ once — the first sight owed to play (§205) was owed because nothing pointed at it.

**Built, on the Fed-chair template — a hold derived from state, not an event:**

- `GameController.HasPendingCampaignOpening()` is true while the player's party has a running campaign whose opening they have not acknowledged (`_campaignOpeningAcknowledgedElection`, the election date of the campaign acknowledged, persisted with the UI draft state). Being a fact about state, the hold survives a load and meets a harness that drives the sim directly.
- It joins the four holds everywhere they are read: the two gates of the day loop, the HELD lamp's `isTimePaused`, and `BuildFoldedInterruptText`, which now names it — *"the opening of your election campaign (Campaign HQ)"* — and names **election night** too when the night's takeover is up, so the banner over the board says what holds the clock rather than whichever meeting waits behind it (the P2-0.2 film's finding).
- **HQ opens itself** the day the campaign begins (`OpenLiveCampaign`, the rail cell's own branch, factored out and also taken by a load that lands on a pending opening), and its masthead carries the interrupt's exit: the **TAKE THE TRAIL** chip, which acknowledges the opening; the clock runs again the next frame. Nothing about the campaign's mechanics moved — the hold is on the clock, not on the campaign.
- Election night was already the takeover after P2-0.2; the film below proves both holds on one played game.

**The film** — `-shotinterrupts`, Sweden, seed 777, both widths (`p2int1280_*.png`, `p2int2560_*.png`; logs `p2int1280.log`, `p2int2560.log`): the driver plays through the controller-shaped day path until the sim has begun the campaign, then lets the controller's own Update meet it. Asserted, each width: the banner names the campaign and HQ has opened itself (`e7a_campaign_opening_hq`); the clock is HELD with the speed set to VeryFast (`SHOT: the clock is HELD on the campaign's opening`); after `AcknowledgeCampaignOpening` the campaign's hold is gone (`e7b_campaign_opening_acknowledged`) - and the frame says why the clock is still held: the harness drove the sim straight to the opening, so the Riksbank appointment, a foreign-policy meeting and the incoming government's budget window had accumulated behind it, each named on the banner in the order the game holds them (in play they are met on their own days); the driver reports that state rather than asserting a running clock, because another interrupt behind this one is legitimate; then the election through `CheckElection`, the night takeover held (`e7c_election_night_takeover`), CONTINUE, and the verdict on the desk (`e7d_…`). A missing interrupt at either point fails the run.

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree (`bar25_p2_0_3_*.log`).

## 220. P2-0.4 — BUDGET BALANCE SHOWS THE YEAR: the annual series, and it sums to the debt delta with every other mover named (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 0): *"The Domestic series becomes annual (per fiscal year); cumulative belongs to debt, which already has its own row. Done when: filmed, and the annual series sums to the debt delta."*

**Before.** `EconomyState.Budget` is an accumulator: every day's balance and every one-time settlement is added to it and nothing ever resets it (`ApplyRevenueAndSpending`, `ApplyOneTimeBudgetImpact`). Two player surfaces printed it as if it were a balance — the Statistics › Domestic headline plate (and through the same readings, the desk strip's BUDGET BALANCE) and the Budget screen's derived row, which at least said "cumulative" in small type. P2-0.1's measurement printed the accumulator beside the year's balance for six countries after two closed years and the two were never the same number; the P2-0.2 film shows the strip carrying it. The sheet's fiscal-position rows were already annual (they read the closed year's report); only the money figure was not.

**Built.**

- `StatHistory.BudgetBalanceAnnual` (with its dates): one point per closed fiscal period, appended where the period closes and the report is written (`SimulationManager`, beside `_lastFiscalReports`). Observation only — nothing reads it back into the model, so the trajectory bar cannot move.
- The Domestic headline reads **the last closed year's balance** from the fiscal report, draws the annual series as its sparkline (the reading had none), and prints a dash before the first close rather than a number no year has computed. The Budget screen's row reads the same figure and says "last closed year" instead of "cumulative". Debt keeps the cumulative, on its own row, as the row said. The accumulator field stays for the model's own delta reading (`PreviewTurn`'s net budget impact) and its doc says it is not a display figure.
- **The harness** is section 4 of `DomesticMoneyBasisDiagnostic` (no new check — R-N5): a fresh world closed one year at a time for every country; after each close the series' newest point IS the report's balance, and the balance IS the debt ledger's flow terms with the sign flipped; over the run the debt delta equals the negated sum of the annual series **plus** the three other stock movers the ledger already attributes — the erosion term, the one-time settlements, and the clamp's truncation — within the ledger's own tolerance idiom. That is the row's done-when stated honestly: the annual series sums to the debt delta once the movers that are not a year's flow are named beside it, and the diagnostic prints them per country every run. The first run, verbatim (`p2_0_4_measure.log`):

```
  USA      debt   35960.0 ->   39454.0  delta  +3494.0 = -sum(annual balance)  +6968.8 + erosion -3474.8 + settlements   +0.0 + clamp   +0.0
  Sweden   debt     217.0 ->     235.2  delta    +18.2 = -sum(annual balance)    +30.8 + erosion   -12.6 + settlements   +0.0 + clamp   +0.0
  Germany  debt    2961.0 ->    3096.9  delta   +135.9 = -sum(annual balance)   +503.7 + erosion  -367.9 + settlements   +0.0 + clamp   +0.0
  France   debt    3712.0 ->    3957.9  delta   +245.9 = -sum(annual balance)   +744.9 + erosion  -498.9 + settlements   +0.0 + clamp   +0.0
  Italy    debt    3174.0 ->    3233.1  delta    +59.1 = -sum(annual balance)   +411.3 + erosion  -352.2 + settlements   +0.0 + clamp   +0.0
  Poland   debt     495.6 ->     634.6  delta   +139.0 = -sum(annual balance)   +168.7 + erosion   -29.6 + settlements   +0.0 + clamp   +0.0
```

## 221. P2-1.1 — NO GAPS: the sheet meets the rail and the window, and the check that could not see the gap under the sheet now can (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 1): *"The sheet meets the rail and the window edge-to-edge: no paper margin, no gap between the rail and the sheet, on every screen. One frame token change, filmed on all screens at the close. Done when: the edge check reports the sheet flush on all four sides."*

**Three literals, not one — and two things the literals uncovered.** The desk margin and the rail-to-sheet gap were the two frame fractions D4 had set to 1.2 %; the third gap was the skin box's own margin, which the paper sheet and the rail both inherit (`_boxStyle`, dressed once) and which adjacent-margin collapse hides but does not remove. All three are zero. The first zero-margin film then showed what the margin had been covering: **a band of desk under the sheet on almost every folded screen**, per tab a different height (15, 21, 33 and 38 px at 720, read off the frames' bottom rows), because the tab sheets opened their paper box with no height and the box ended where each tab's own scroll arithmetic ended. Sizing the five tab boxes to the frame removed those and left **exactly 4 px on every screen that carries the hold banner** and none on the screens without one — the banner's measured height (`DrawFoldedInterruptBanner`'s return) runs 4 px over what the layout consumes. Rather than argue the margin-collapse arithmetic, the frame now fills by construction: the content column takes the frame's height and every sheet — the five tabs, the desk stage, the eight campaign stages — expands into it (`GUILayout.ExpandHeight`), so no measurement stands between the banner and the bottom edge. The inner scroll arithmetic is untouched; paper rather than desk fills whatever it leaves.

**The edge check, twice re-derived.** `ScreenEdgeCheck` sampled its desk reference at pixel (1,1), "outside the margin by construction" — at zero margin that pixel is the rail and every verdict flips; the reference is now `PoliSimTheme.Desk`, the one statement of what the ground is. And its zero-margin verdict is the row's done-when made strict: a side is flush when its edge run **covers** the line (`FullLineFraction`), not when it exceeds the clip test's 20 px — the rail is content down the whole left column and along the bottom row's first cells whatever the sheet does, so the 20 px rule called the 33 px band flush on the first pass, which is the class this check exists for; the strict rule found the 4 px residue on the second. Some sides flush and others not is a gap; no side flush is a takeover on the ground (the country selector, the saves menu) and stays a background by the check's existing symmetry rule. The frame's dimensions come out of the analyser so the rule is stated in fractions.

**A probe in the frame.** On Repaint the frame compares the sheet's bottom with the column's and logs any difference with its size (`FRAME: the sheet ends N px short of the frame`), so a film carries the number. On the flush frame it reports nothing for the sheets — and two overflows the other way, which are clips, not gaps, and pre-date this row: the **Budget** sheet runs some 260 px past the frame at 720 even when it expands, because a box cannot be shorter than its content and the three-column body is taller than a 720 window (the Estimated Effects horizon buttons are what the frame cuts, and P2-2.1 retires them; at 1440 it fits exactly), and **Policy Laws** runs 9 px past it on four sub-screens at 720. Both are recorded here for the rows that own them.

**The film:** every screen, Sweden, seed 777, 1280 and 2560 (`p2gap1280_*.png`, `p2gap2560_*.png`; logs `p2gap1280.log`, `p2gap2560.log`): the driver's own exit runs the edge check over the run's films (M-S16) with the strict rule — clean — and reading every frame's bottom row (the measurement this section made by hand three times) finds a band only on the takeovers that stand on the ground by design.

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree (`bar27_p2_1_1_*.log`).

## 222. P2-1.2 — CONTRAST, ROUND TWO: every ink pair at its real use, derived from the tokens on every run (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 1): *"D6 aimed at 4.5:1 and two targets missed (Caution 4.09/3.90, TextPrimary-on-brass 4.03). Re-measure every ink pair at its real size after P2-1.1, and raise the faint inks until every body-text pair clears 4.5 and every caption pair clears 3.5. Token values only; if a target cannot be met without a new hue, that pair goes to Design. Done when: the measured table is in the record with no pair below its floor."*

**The measurement reproduces the sheet's figures exactly** — Caution on the sheet 4.09, on the tile 3.90, TextPrimary on brass 4.03 — from the theme's hex literals through WCAG 2.x relative luminance, which is the arithmetic D6 was checked with. The two D6 misses are **caption** uses at 8.5–9 px (the BREAKING chip, the threshold labels, the selected chip's caption), and against the row's own floor for captions (3.5) both clear; so does every other caption pair on every paper ground, and every body pair of the three text inks. **The pairs that did not clear were not the ones the sheet named:** the area inks — drawn as body text in section headers, ledger names and the `DeskBody` ladder — sit on the sheet at 3.59 (Trade), 3.60 (Labor), 3.84 (Neutral), 4.07 (Political), 4.24 (Welfare), 4.27 (Infrastructure), 4.31 (Global) and 4.41 (SovereignWealth); Fiscal, CrimeJustice and Sectors clear. D6 had darkened two of them (Global, Political) to a 4.0 target for 16 px labels; the row's body floor is 4.5.

**Raised, hue held, token values only.** Each failing area ink is scaled toward black in sRGB — hue and saturation held in HSV terms, the D6 method's intent without its oklch tooling — to the first hex that clears 4.5 with a rounding margin; the derivation is the table the check prints, and the new values are in `UiPalette`'s area table with the old ones beside them in the diff. ⚠ These inks are also FILLS (tab tints, washes, bars); the fills darken with them, as D6's Global and Political did. No pair needed a new hue, so nothing goes to Design from this row; D10's row 9 stays empty.

**Two more the census caught that the sheet did not name.** `Good` as body text on the plate inset sat at 4.37 and is raised the same way (`#2E7048` → the value in `PoliSimTheme`, hue held). And the deltas: `GetDeltaColor` prints every delta in `UiPalette`'s own `PositiveChangeColor`, which was the **pre-D6** green D6 had measured at 3.4 and darkened only in the theme — the copy that every delta actually prints in never moved. The three delta colours are now assignments of the theme's verdict tokens (`Good`, `Bad`, `TextSecondary`), so the two cannot drift again, and the check lists them.

**The instrument.** `InkContrastCheck` (cheap suite; R-N5's second cost is this row — the first was D6's hand re-measure missing two pairs) enumerates the ink-on-ground pairs the UI draws as text, each with the floor its use sets, derives the ratio from the theme tokens at run time, prints the table and fails any pair below its floor. A ratio may only rise. The table is the record's, by pointer: `InkContrastCheck.Run`'s output in any bar log from this commit on.

**The film:** the sweep at 1280 and 2560 carries the darkened area inks on every screen (`p2ink1280_*.png`, `p2ink2560_*.png`).

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree, the new check among them (`bar28_p2_1_2_*.log`).

## 223. P2-1.3 — THE BUDGET SLIDERS: a longer, thinner track, a step the track can carry, the prose above the rows cut, and reach proven on every film (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 1): *"Longer track, thinner height, finer step; the description texts under each slider cut (the (b)/(c) taxonomy applied to Budget). Done when: filmed, and a slider can be set to any whole percentage point without overshoot."*

**What the row was drawing.** Every Budget row is a `LedgerRow`: name, track, the figure pair, the trailing text, and on the tax rows a verdict column and the Remove button beside it. The fixed columns took 56 % of the row before the track was given what was left, the verdict and action columns another 28 % of the tax row outside it, the track drew at 15 reference px, and the knob was the skin thumb at 3.5 % of the window's height. **Measured on the first reach film at 1280** (`p2sl1280.log`, the first pass): a Budget track covered up to 1.37 units per pixel — the Carbon Tax's 0–100 range on some seventy pixels — and the value was continuous, printed to two decimals, so a whole point was something the thumb passed through and the row showed digits no hand had set.

**Built.**

- **Longer:** the fixed columns take less (`LedgerRow.Columns`: name 26 → 18 %, figure 19 → 13 %, trailing 11 → 8 %, the need caps 34 → 22 %), and on the tax rows the verdict and Remove columns 13 + 15 → 11 + 12 %; the track is the remainder. The name cell gained a width need — its widest unbreakable token, up to 30 % — because the first narrower column overflowed on a hyphenated party name at 17 px that cannot wrap (`Arbetarepartiet-Socialdemokraterna`, five Politics and Laws frames), the way the figure and trailing cells already had theirs.
- **Thinner:** the bar at 8 reference px (from 15), the knob at 2 % of the window's height (clamped 14–28 px) and a narrower thumb (12–24 px), one place for the ledger rows and the standalone rate sliders alike.
- **A step the track can carry.** The draft snaps, and the step adapts to the track (`LedgerRow.StepFor`): a tenth of a unit where a unit has ten pixels, a half where it has two, else the whole unit. ⚠ A fixed tenth was the first cut and the measurement retired it: at 1280 no Budget track has ten pixels to the point, so a tenth would have been a promise the pixels could not keep. The rule that holds at every width is that **a whole unit is always a resting value** — that is the row's done-when — and the step is as fine beyond it as the track allows.
- **The prose cut,** by the taxonomy: the Budget header's paragraph restating the screen ((b): the sub-tabs and the columns say it) and the three mechanism paragraphs above the Tax, Spending and Welfare rows ((c): the hatched draft, the figure pair, the WOULD PASS verdict and the standalone Remove say it). The bill-status line and the Introduce button stay: a status is not a description. `BudgetProcessDescription` stays as the record of the cut text; the header's height measure no longer counts it.

**Reach, proven on every film (no new check — R-N5).** While the capture harness is armed, `LedgerRow.Draw` records for every interactive row the range a pixel of its track covers; the driver clears the record as each capture begins and collects it after the frame is written (so a row drawn while the driver scrolls toward the next screen is never filed under the previous stem — the first keying did exactly that and filed a Policy Laws dial under a Budget stem), and records on Repaint only - on the Layout event `GUILayoutUtility.GetRect` hands the row a dummy rect, the columns squeeze to their minimum, and the second film kept that ghost as the Carbon Tax row's worst (73 px, exactly the minimum track) while the frame showed a track twice as long - and at its exit **fails the run** if any row on a Budget frame (the `05*` stems) covers more than a whole unit per pixel, the bound under which some pixel rests on every whole value. The worst row over every frame is reported beside it for the record (the Policy Web node panel's dial, which the first films named as the worst at 1.4 weeks per pixel, was the same Layout ghost; on Repaint the worst row anywhere is a Budget one). On the films that closed the row, the worst Budget row is the Means-Tested Welfare generosity at 1280 - under the bound, and at a whole-unit step; at 2560 the same row rests on half units. The numbers are in every film's log (`SHOT: slider reach on the Budget - …`), read from the real layout at the real width rather than a duplicate of the column arithmetic.

**The film:** the sweep at 1280 and 2560 (`p2sl1280_*.png`, `p2sl2560_*.png`; the reach lines in `p2sl1280.log` and `p2sl2560.log`), the Budget sub-screens among them.

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree (`bar29_p2_1_3_*.log`).

## 224. P2-1.4 — THE PERSISTENT FISCAL HEADER ON BUDGET: five derived readings in the chip-strip idiom, outside the columns' scroll (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 1): *"Balance, debt, debt-to-GDP, revenue and spending totals visible at all times on the Budget screen, derived, in the chip-strip idiom. Done when: filmed in scrolled and unscrolled states."*

**Built.** The desk's chip strip is now an idiom rather than a method: `DrawChipStrip(rect, readings)` draws whatever reading list it is handed, the desk hands it the headline set as before, and the Budget hands it `BuildFiscalReadings()` — the closed year's balance (with the annual series as its line, P2-0.4's), the debt stock, the debt-to-GDP ratio (with its quarterly line), and the closed year's revenue and total spending, each from the fiscal report or the live state, a dash before the first close. The strip sits in the Budget's header, above the three columns and outside their scroll, at the desk strip's own board height scaled by the window (one strip, one size); the header's height measure counts it so the columns below are reserved against it.

**One residue of P2-1.3, found on this row's first film and fixed here.** With the narrower figure cell the standing and draft figures on the Spending rows printed touching (`$10.5B$10.1B`): `LedgerRow.DrawFigurePair` right-aligned both halves of the cell with nothing between them. A gap between the halves, scaled with the type, is the difference between a pair and a smear; the second film carries it.

**The film:** the Budget's five sub-screens at 1280 and 2560, at scroll zero and scrolled to the rows and deeper (`p2fh1280_05*.png`, `p2fh2560_05*.png`) — the strip is on every frame.

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree (`bar30_p2_1_4_*.log`).

## 225. P2-2.1 — THE 1D/1W/1M/1Y HORIZONS RETIRED: the effects panel is the budget delta and an arrow per outcome the draft moves (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 2): *"Retire the 1D/1W/1M/1Y horizons. The effects panel becomes: the budget delta on the right, always; and as a slider moves, the affected categories surface with an arrow per category — direction up/down, length scaled by estimated magnitude, colour by the existing direction-aware `GetDeltaColor` … Ranges never false precision — the deterministic preview's point with its scope stated (C-C1's precedent). Done when: filmed in rest and mid-drag states, and every arrow's length traces to the preview's own figure."*

**What the horizons were.** `PreviewTurn` produces one full-turn projection. Since the Continuous Time Migration's Phase 0 the panel had rescaled it four ways for display — a day, a week, a month, the year — by simple proportion (compounding for GDP), behind four buttons on the Budget and four chips on the Desk's effects card, with sixteen cached copies of eight figures. Four numbers for one fact, three of them arithmetic on the fourth, and the default the smallest: a day's slice of a year's projection printed to two decimals.

**Built.**

- **Retired:** the `PreviewHorizon` enum, its day counts and labels, the two rescaling functions, the sixteen scaled fields, the Budget's four buttons and the Desk card's four chips (the card's chip now names the scope, NEXT YEAR, and its eight rows read the full-turn figures the Statistics projections already read).
- **The panel:** the budget delta stands above it in the same column as before (`DrawBudgetDraftFiscalImpact` — revenue, spending, net, and the scope sentence C-C1 set). Beneath it, `EffectArrowsRenderer`: one column per outcome the draft moves — the figure at the head, the arrow up for a rise and down for a fall, its length the effect's magnitude against the largest on the panel (`length = lane × |value| / max|value|`, the figure at the head being the value the length was scaled from), its ink `GetDeltaColor(value, higherIsBetter)`, the outcome's name at the foot. An outcome whose figure would print as zero is not on the panel — that is how "the affected categories surface as a slider moves" is read: what the draft does not move is not drawn. With nothing drafted the panel says so in one sentence.
- **Scope, once, in one line:** the impact block's four-line sentence ("A full year, from the model's own boundary run twice…") is one line now - *"Next year, the model's own boundary run with and without this draft - deterministic, no margin, no events."* - and it covers the delta above it and the arrows below it. The first film at 720 showed why: with two sentences the arrows sat below the fold of the Budget's right column, which already runs past a 720 frame (§221's finding); with one they fit. The same 720 frame also asked for the column's three headers to be one line each - "Support (current draft)", "Budget impact", "Effects" - the (b)-class trim of Track 1 applied to the words "Legislative", "Estimated" and "on the year's budget", which the lines beneath each header already say. The verdict pair became one line the same way ("Bill direction: Expansionary (+30,0) · WOULD FAIL"), and the scope sentence lost the words "the model's own boundary" - the second film still cut the arrows' foot by the column's last few dozen pixels at 720, and these were the words left that said nothing the line beside them did not.

**The film:** the Budget at rest, before the driver drafts a line (`p2aw1280_05r_budget_rest.png`, `p2aw2560_05r_budget_rest.png` — the idle sentence), and mid-draft with the drafted spending lines (`p2ar*_05*_budget_*.png` — the arrows). The lengths trace by construction: the renderer has no other input than the list the preview filled.

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree (`bar31_p2_2_1_*.log`).

**The lanes.** The first framed film split two captions inside a word at 1280 ("Unemploy / ment", "participatio / n"): six equal lanes were narrower than the longest word. The lanes are now sized by each caption's widest word (and its figure), the slack shared equally, so a word never breaks; only when the words alone exceed the column would the lanes fall back to equal shares, and then the overflow guard reports it. (`EffectArrowsRenderer.Draw`.)

## 226. P2-2.2 — PARLIAMENTARY SUPPORT AS SEATS: every mandate coloured for, against or undecided, from the one enumeration the verdict reads (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 2): *"The hemicycle in the Budget preview colours each mandate for/against/undecided, computed from the parties' stances on the draft; the same component replaces the lean bar on every law-support preview. Done when: the per-seat map's counts equal the existing stance arithmetic to the seat, on Budget and on Laws."*

**What the lean bar said.** `UiPalette.DrawDivergingBar` filled from a centre line toward the sign of the seat-weighted alignment — one number, the chamber's stances weighted by seats and summed, which is what the verdict (`WouldBillPass`) reads. A bar of that number says how far the chamber leans and nothing about which mandates make it lean; the Laws page's party list already said which parties sit FOR, AGAINST, UNALIGNED or UNMEASURED by the sign of their stance times the bill's direction.

**Built.**

- **One enumeration.** `ParliamentSystem.SeatSides(country, direction, axis)` yields every seated party with its seats, its side (+1 FOR when its stance times the bill's sign is positive, −1 AGAINST when negative, 0 UNDECIDED when it has no measured position on the axis or its stance is exactly neutral — the Laws page's rule), its weight and whether it is measured. `GetSeatWeightedAlignment` now sums its weights from the same enumeration, so the map's counts and the verdict's arithmetic cannot drift: they are one loop read twice.
- **The map.** `SeatMapRenderer`: a compact hemicycle sized to the rect it is given — every seat a dot on concentric half-rings, FOR on the left in the Good ink, UNDECIDED in the middle in the muted ink, AGAINST on the right in the Bad ink — with the counts beneath (FOR · UNDECIDED · AGAINST · OF the chamber). It replaces the lean bar in the shared law-support preview (`DrawBillLiveEstimate`, which the Budget, Labor, Trade and Sectors previews and the Desk's docket card draw through) and in the Parliament page's pending-law card; the division records' bars stay, being history of an alignment as it was recorded.
- **The proof.** A clause in `OfficeTestDiagnostic` (simulation group; no new check — R-N5): for every country, both axes and both bill directions, the sides list every seat the chamber holds, each party's side is the sign of its stance times the bill's sign, and the alignment re-summed from the enumeration equals the one the verdict reads. Printed per country and direction on every run.

**The film:** the Budget's preview column mid-draft and at rest, and the Desk's docket card, at 1280 and 2560 (`p2sm1280_05b_budget_spending.png`, `p2sm1280_05r_budget_rest.png`, `p2sm1280_01c_desk.png`, `p2sm2560_…`): 82 captures each, 0 overflows, 0 edge clips, 0 containment escapes, and the Budget sheet inside a 720 frame again (the first film with the map had it 98 px over).

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree (`bar32_p2_2_2_*.log`).

**What the first films taught.** Four fixed rings of nine-pixel dots merged 349 mandates into bands - the very fault P2-3.1 names on the Politics page - so the map now finds its rings the way the rewritten hemicycle will: the fewest rings (from three) whose combined arc length seats every mandate at a dot-and-a-third pitch, the dots sized from the ring gap. The caption had been allotted a line height shorter than its measured height (121 overflows across the two films, all that one caption), so its height is measured with `CalcSize`, and it lost its "OF n" clause when it ran 4,5 px past the Budget column at 1280 - the chamber total is the sum, and the Politics banner states it. The map's radius is capped at 4,2 font sizes: a preview column at 720 has to keep its verdict, its budget delta, its scope and its arrows in frame beneath it, and to make that room the verdict line lost its "Bill direction:" prefix, the three budget-impact lines became one (the net alone carrying the colour, as before), the scope sentence shortened to "Next year, with vs without this draft. No events.", the arrows' lane shrank half a font size and two stacked spaces above "Effects" (with a note about the retired horizon buttons) became one. `ParliamentSystem.SeatSides` treats a zero direction as no side: Unity's `Mathf.Sign(0f)` is 1, and the pending-law card used to guard its bar with its own contested flag; now an unopposed bill maps every seat UNDECIDED and the alignment for it is 0 rather than the chamber's raw stances.

## 227. P2-3.1 — THE HEMICYCLE DRAWS SEATS: rings chosen for the width so every mandate is a distinct dot, parties by bloc then mandates, the legend grouped, the dot count held to the chamber (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 3): *"Individual mandates, not curved bands - 349 dots for Sweden, party-coloured, sorted by bloc then by mandates. Party list sorted by mandates with the blocs drawn as groups (W-D3's bloc data). Done when: filmed, and the dot count equals the chamber."*

**What the old hemicycle did.** Five fixed rows twenty pixels apart, ten-pixel dots, a 340×190 area whatever the sheet - 349 seats on five short arcs means a dot every three pixels, and the dots merged into the curved bands the row names. The parties ran left to right by each one's published CHES `lrecon` (W-G1), the legend in the same order.

**Built.**

- **Rings by capacity.** `HemicycleRenderer` sizes its arc from the type (a radius of fourteen font sizes, or half the width if that is less) and finds the fewest rings, from four, whose combined arc length seats every mandate at a pitch of a dot and a third, the dot sized from the ring gap; seats per ring in proportion to its radius, the outermost taking the rounding remainder. For Sweden's chamber at 1280 that is ten rings of roughly eight-pixel dots with air between them; at 2560 the same geometry doubled. A soft-edged 32-pixel dot texture keeps a downscaled dot round.
- **Bloc order.** `NationalElection.BlocOf(country, abbrev)` reads the 2022 table the tactical-voting model already carries for Sweden (`SwedenBlocs2022`: 0 the left bloc - S, V, C, MP; 1 the right bloc - M, KD, L, SD) and answers −1 for every other chamber and any party outside the table; `BlocName` names them as the election night film does. The dots run left to right by bloc rank (left, unaffiliated, right) and within a bloc by mandates, ties by abbreviation; the legend lists the parties in the same order, with a header per group ("THE LEFT BLOC · 173 SEATS", the seats summed from the same dictionary the dots read) wherever the chamber has bloc data, and no headers where it has none - absence, not an invented grouping.
- **The count, held.** The renderer records the dots it drew, the seats the dictionary summed to and the chamber the party system declares on every Repaint; `UiScreenshotDriver.Capture` reads them on each parliament capture and logs `SHOT: hemicycle drew N dot(s) on R ring(s) for a chamber of N seat(s) (declared N)`, counting a failure when the three differ. The ladder's caption for this instrument says what now sizes it.

**The film:** `p2hc1280_07a_politics_parliament.png`, `p2hc2560_07a_politics_parliament.png` - 82 captures each, 0 overflows, 0 edge clips; the tally line reads 349 dots on ten rings for a chamber of 349, declared 349, at both widths.

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` clean; `RunAllBatch` failed its first run on `UnwiredSubsystemCheck` - the renderer's new `ArcHeight` helper was public and called only from its own file, an uncalled entry point above the recorded ceiling - and ran clean once it was private (`bar33_p2_3_1_*.log`; the simulation bar's run predates that one-word visibility change and nothing it measures can see it).

**Left as found.** The sourced Swedish party inks give the four right-bloc parties near-identical blues at dot size, so the right bloc reads as one colour on the arc; the legend's swatches separate them. That is the ink table's question (Design's D-8.2 palette), not this row's.

## 228. P2-3.2 — THE COMPASS CONVERTS: CHES lrecon × galtan on fixed scales, parties at their published pairs, countries and the cabinet at seat-weighted means, every point traced (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 3): *"Axes become CHES `lrecon` (economic left–right) × `galtan` (liberal–conservative), both wired at F5 with endpoints read. Parties at their published positions; a country at the seat-weighted mean of its chamber; the government's point marked. Axis labels in the conventional words. Done when: every point traces to a CHES row or a seat-weighted derivation, no authored position anywhere."*

**What the compass plotted before.** Two blends of the game's own policy data - "fiscal size" (the average implemented tax rate with spending as a share of GDP) and "regulation & welfare" (average sector regulation with the generosity of implemented welfare) - auto-scaled to the six countries' observed spread and padded, so the plot was a spread of readings of what each government does, and Playtest 3's finding that it "only appears to operate on the x-axis" was a model fact (§P finding 1: the six Y values within one axis unit). Nothing on it was a position anyone had published.

**Built.**

- **The scales.** `CompassPositions` (Elections) is the one source of every point: a party's own published pair (`PoliticalParty.LrEcon`, `.Galtan` - CHES 2024, 0 left / GAL … 10 right / TAN, the endpoints the codebook gives and F5 wired), null where either is NaN; a chamber's seat-weighted mean over the seated parties that publish both, with the seats that could not count returned beside it; a cabinet's seat-weighted mean over its members. `PoliticalCompassRenderer` plots on the fixed 0–10 scales - a point's place is its value, not its rank among six - with the end words at the plot's edges (LEFT / RIGHT, LIBERAL (GAL) / CONSERVATIVE (TAN)) and the axis captions naming the CHES variables.
- **Three kinds of point.** The player's chamber's parties, small, in the neutral ink (D9 row 5: party ink never sits beside an area accent, and the countries are drawn in theirs), tagged by abbreviation; each of the six countries at its chamber's mean, in the country's ink, named, the player's ringed; the player's sitting cabinet as a hollow ring in the country's ink, tagged "cabinet". The other five countries' parties are not drawn - six chambers of party dots in six ink tables on one square would say nothing - and the legend column beside the plot says exactly what is drawn and what each point rests on, including the seats a mean had to leave out.
- **The cabinet, without the player.** `GovernmentFormation.Form` needed the player's party to answer at all; the formation itself did not. It is now `TryFormChamber` (seats, derived compatibility, declared red lines, the chamber's own rule), shared by `Form` - unchanged in what it returns, including "the player holds no party" - and the new `Cabinet(country)`, which lists the sitting cabinet's parties whether or not the player holds one, empty when the chamber forms no government.
- **The old axes, kept where they were read.** The two policy blends moved to `PolicyStanceAxes` (Simulation) because the Statistics comparison still prints them for two countries, now labelled "Policy stance" rather than "Compass"; `CompassAxisDiagnostic`, whose subject was the old Y axis's collapse, is deleted with its subject.
- **The proof.** A clause in `OfficeTestDiagnostic` (simulation group; no new check - R-N5): for every country, each party point is its own published pair or absent exactly when a scale is NaN; the chamber mean re-summed from seats × pairs equals `ChamberMean` and its seats-left-out equals the seated unpaired; the cabinet mean re-summed over `Cabinet`'s members equals `CabinetMean`, and is absent exactly when no member publishes a pair. Printed per country on every run.

**The film:** the Compass tab and the Desk's compass card at 1280 and 2560 (`p2cp1280_07b_politics_compass.png`, `p2cp1280_01c_desk.png`, `p2cp2560_…`).

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree (`bar34_p2_3_2_*.log`).

**What the first film taught.** With every point on one small square the six chamber means - all within a unit of one another on both scales, which is itself the finding - put six country names on top of each other, and the plot at 720 was 288 px wide. The renderer now has two modes. With a legend (the Compass tab) the plot takes the height the sheet has and a column beside it names every point with its pair and the seats it rests on: the six countries (with the seats that publish no pair, where a chamber has them - France's 260 of 317), the cabinet (its members, their seat-weighted mean, their seats) and the player's parties (each pair, or "no published pair"); the plot keeps only the party abbreviations and the "cabinet" tag as text. Without one (the Desk card, the ladder) the plot carries the six dots, the player's ring and name and the two axis captions, and nothing else - the first compact film had the caption wrapped at the plot's width but measured at the card's and escaping the card by 9 px on every Desk capture; the captions now wrap at the width the footprint measured them at. Design's compass r2 board (P2-3.3's note) can refine this composition; the data and the legend ship now.

**A finding the ring makes visible (for the report).** The cabinet ring draws whatever `GovernmentFormation` forms, and outside Sweden the formation runs without declared red lines (W-D3: "declared red lines are sourced for Sweden only"). The diagnostic's print shows what that yields at the seed: Germany's cabinet formed as CDU+AfD+CSU and France's as ENS+RN+LR - coalitions the real chambers exclude by declaration, which the model does not know for those countries. The compass reports the model faithfully; the gap is the red-line sourcing for five chambers, W-D3's own open question, now with a screen that shows it.

**What the bar taught.** The cheap bar's first run failed two checks. `ConstantProvenanceCheck`: the two clamp bounds that moved with the policy blends from the UI into `PolicyStanceAxes` had crossed onto the simulation path unmarked - they are now marked CONVENTION (the 0–100 display scale the blends are clamped to). `PartyInkDrawSiteCheck`: the compass had become a second draw site for party ink, beside the countries' accent inks - D9 row 5's rule is that party ink never sits beside an area accent, and the country colours are area accents - so the party dots and their legend swatches are drawn in the neutral ink, identified by their tags; the hemicycle stays the one surface where a party's identity is the subject. Both films were re-shot after the ink change.

## 229. P2-3.3 — THE COMPASS GAINS HISTORY AND THE ELECTORATE: a trail per chamber stored at every close and drawn as stored, the electorate at the compatibility-weighted mean of the parties election night predicts from (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 3): *"A trail of each country's point over time (it moves at elections and government changes — store it per turn, draw it faint); and the electorate's position from the voter groups over the cohorts (F3's substrate: the eligible population's compatibility-weighted mean). Design's compass r2 board refines the composition; the data ships now. Done when: the trail reproduces the stored history exactly and the electorate point derives from cohorts."*

**Built.**

- **The trail, stored.** `StatHistory` carries three parallel lists - `CompassTrailLrEcon`, `CompassTrailGaltan`, `CompassTrailDates` - and `SimulationManager` appends the chamber's seat-weighted mean (`CompassPositions.RecordTrailPoint`) at every turn close, beside the fiscal report and the annual balance point. Three floats and a date rather than a `Vector2`, because the save serializes the world whole and a `Vector2`'s self-referential properties trip the serializer; a chamber with no mean appends nothing. The trail persists with the save because the history does.
- **The trail, drawn.** `CompassPositions.Trail(country)` zips the three lists in order, nothing dropped, nothing smoothed; the renderer draws that list as a faint polyline with a small dot at each stored point in the country's ink, beneath the live points, on both the Compass tab and the Desk card. The legend states how many points are stored for the player's chamber and their dates; before the first close it says the trail starts at the first close. A trail with one point is not drawn - a point is not a path.
- **The electorate.** `CompassPositions.ElectorateMean(country)` weights each positioned party's published pair by its compatibility on the vote model's good layer - the arrays `NationalElection.TryCompatibility` returns, the same ones election night predicts from and the campaign is staged on, the fitted electorate over the cohorts (F3's substrate) - and returns the mean with the number of parties that carried weight; null where no electorate is fitted or no two-election history exists (absence, not a centre). The plot draws it as a filled diamond in the primary ink, tagged "electorate", a shape no other point uses; the legend states the pair and the party count, or that no electorate is fitted for this chamber. The fitted electorate's own centre (`VoteModel.Electorate.MuEcon`/`MuSoc`) is a different object - the model's fitted centre on its own two axes - and is not drawn; the row asks for the derivation from the cohorts' compatibility.
- **The proof.** Two clauses, in existing diagnostics (R-N5). `OfficeTestDiagnostic` (simulation group): for every country, the electorate point re-derived from `TryCompatibility`'s own arrays equals `ElectorateMean` to four decimals, with the same party count, and is absent exactly where no electorate is fitted. `DomesticMoneyBasisDiagnostic` (simulation group, the four-closed-years run): every chamber with a mean carries exactly one trail point per closed year, dated at the close and in order; the newest equals the chamber mean recomputed now; and the list the compass draws is the stored lists element for element.

**The film:** the Compass tab and the Desk card at 1280 and 2560 (`p2ct1280_07b_politics_compass.png`, `p2ct1280_01c_desk.png`, `p2ct2560_…`). The sweep advances the clock, so the legend on film already counts stored points with their dates; the four-year diagnostic is where the trail's content is proved.

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree (`bar35_p2_3_3_*.log`).

## 230. P2-3.4 — THE RIKSBANK PANEL: the rate today, the rule's inputs as readings, and the projected path as the rule on the preview's projection, asserted (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 3): *"More of what the model holds: the current rate, the reaction function's inputs (the model's inflation and output readings), and the projected rate path from the Taylor rule applied to the preview's projection — derived, with the scope stated. Done when: the projected path equals the rule evaluated on the projection, asserted."*

**What the panel held.** With a sitting chair: the rule's reading today with its inputs in a note, the chair's lean, the chair's target, the appointment modal and the rate's history graph. The rate itself appeared only as the graph's last point; the output gap the model computes was not shown; nothing looked forward.

**Built.**

- **The projection's readings.** `PolicyPreview` now carries the previewed year's end readings the rule reads - inflation, unemployment, the natural rate, the output gap - the rule's reading on them (`PreviewRuleRate`, `TaylorRule.GetSuggestedInterestRate` on the previewed clone at its year's end) and the rate the previewed year ran at. The preview is the one the Budget's effects already come from: the current draft applied for one deterministic year, no margin, no events.
- **The path.** `RatePathProjection.Project(country, preview)` (Simulation): three steps for a country with a sitting chair - the rate today; after this year's move, the chair closing `FederalReserveSystem.RateAdjustmentSpeed` of the gap to a target that is the rule on today's readings plus the lean, clamped to the band (exactly `ApplyFedChairInterestRate`'s arithmetic); after next year's move toward the same target arithmetic on the preview's reading. Nothing beyond the preview's year is forecast, and the panel says so. Null without a chair (a currency-zone member, or a rate the player sets), so those branches of the panel are unchanged.
- **The panel.** Above the appointment modal: "Policy rate now"; "Rule inputs" with inflation against the country's target, unemployment against NAIRU with the gap in points, and the output gap as a reading the rule does not weigh (it weighs the unemployment gap - the panel says which); then "Projected path" - three rows, each with its rule reading, target and basis - and a scope sentence carrying the preview's readings and the chair's speed. The controller keeps the whole `PolicyPreview` it already computes for the Budget (`_cachedPreview`), recomputed on the same turn-change rule, so the panel adds no second projection.
- **The proof.** A clause in `PreviewParityDiagnostic` - which joins the simulation group this pass: it had been a standalone diagnostic no bar ran, the unwired-proof trap R-N5 exists to close (R-N5): for every country with a sitting chair, the preview's rule reading re-derived from the rule's own formula on the preview's readings equals `PreviewRuleRate`; the path's three rates are the target arithmetic and the adjustment speed applied twice from the rate today; the targets are the readings plus the lean, clamped; and the previewed year ran at the target on today's readings. Printed per country on every run.

**The film:** the Riksbank tab at 1280 and 2560 (`p2rb1280_07d_politics_federalreserve.png`, `p2rb2560_…`).

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` - eleven checks now, `PreviewParityDiagnostic` enrolled - and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree (`bar36_p2_3_4_*.log`); the parity log prints the path for the three chambers with a sitting chair (the USA, Sweden, Poland).

**What the film taught.** The derived-stat row's trailing lane is a fixed share of the sheet, and the first notes beside the path's figures ran to twice it at 1280 (twelve overflows across the Riksbank captures); the rows now carry the figures - the rule reading, the target and whose readings they rest on - and the scope sentence beneath carries the sentences.

## 231. P2-4.1 — EVERY SCREEN FILMED AS ELIAS SAW IT, at 1280 / 1600 / 2560, with the dead-space measure per screen (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 4): *"Film every screen as Elias saw it at 1280/1600/2560 after Track 1 lands, with the dead-space measure per screen, as the annex."*

**The measure.** `ScreenEdgeCheck`, which already reads every capture a pass writes for the edge guard, now also counts the frame's dead space: the share of pixels within the content threshold of a ground - the desk, the paper, the tile (`PoliSimTheme.Desk`, `Card`, `Tile`) - which is what nothing is drawn on. It prints the share on every capture's edge line (`dead nn.n%`) and closes the pass with `=== Dead space: mean … emptiest: …` naming the five emptiest captures. A measure for the annex, not a verdict: no threshold, no failure - the board reads it beside the film, and a paper page dense with type still reads mostly as ground at this threshold, so the figure is "how much of the frame is bare", not "how much is useful".

**The geometry the harness accepts.** The first attempt filmed 1600×900 and was refused: the harness holds the project's four filmed geometries (S-17: 1280×720, 1600×950, 1920×1080, 2560×1440) and an off-standard height is a discrepancy, not a choice. The middle width is 1600×950.

**The films** (`p2an1280_*.png`, `p2an1600_*.png`, `p2an2560_*.png` - the same eighty-two stems at each width, at HEAD after Track 3): 82 captures each, 0 overflows, 0 edge clips, 0 containment escapes; the frame probe's one standing entry is the PolicyLaws sheet 9 px past a 720 frame (pre-existing). Mean dead space over the pass: 75,7% at 1280, 76,6% at 1600, 78,5% at 2560 - the wider the frame, the more of it is bare, which is the sitting's own finding measured.

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree (`bar37_p2_4_1_*.log`).

## 233. P2-4.3 — THE STRUCTURAL HALVES THAT NEED NO BOARD: the law-result and election-result screens full-frame with their content, the Docket's minister alerts and per-option cost-and-impact arrows (2026-09-02)

**The row** (`POLISIM_FEATURE_LIST.md` P2, Track 4): *"The law-result and election-result screens get their full-frame content now (per-seat vote map from P2-2.2, effect arrows from P2-2.1, the attribution ledger), in the v3 idiom; the Docket gets a minister-alerts region fed by whatever the cabinet already emits. Boards refine. Done when: filmed, nothing is a square on black."*

**What stood.** The signing ceremony was an 820×680 document centred over the scrim - a square on black at every width above 1280 - carrying the bill's title, a lean bar of the recorded alignment and the seal. Election night was a 1240×720 document, the same way. The Docket listed what was waiting as cards; a cabinet decision's options were buttons with no figure beside them.

**Built.**

- **The division carries its vote.** `DivisionRecord` gains the bill's direction and axis and every party's side with its seats (`DivisionSide`), recorded by `ParliamentSystem.RecordDivision` from `SeatSides` - the enumeration the verdict read - at the moment of the division, so the ceremony draws the vote as it was and not the chamber as it is later; the trade bill now names its axis when it records (its recorded alignment is the openness-axis figure the verdict used, where it was the fiscal one). It also carries the estimate (`DivisionEffect`): the controller snapshots the preview's arrows as the turn closes (the decision that became the bill) and attaches them to every division that turn resolved when it queues the ceremony. Divisions from before this pass have neither, and the screen says so rather than drawing zeros.
- **The instruments as textures.** `CanvasPaint` paints the per-seat map (P2-2.2's rings by capacity, FOR left, UNDECIDED middle, AGAINST right) and the effect arrows (P2-2.1's lanes from a baseline, length by size relative to the largest, ink by whether the move is good) into a `Texture2D` once, for the retained-mode Canvas screens, with the renderers' own rules - the two surfaces cannot disagree about what a division or an estimate looks like.
- **The signing ceremony, full-frame.** The document and its shadow anchor to the frame with a margin of scrim around them at every width; the plate that held the lean bar is three panels in a row - THE DIVISION (the map and the counts), THE CITATION (the division number, the date, the alignment and CARRIED / LOST, the axis) and THE ESTIMATE (the arrows and their figures) - at a height that takes a share of the frame. The v3 idiom stands: paper, hairlines, the ornate frame, the seal and the brass button.
- **Election night, full-frame, with the ledger.** The document anchors to the frame the same way, and the side column gains WHY — {PARTY}, LINE BY LINE: the campaign's attribution ledger (W-E7's sources, largest lines first, in points), from `SimulationManager.PlayerCampaignLedger` - `VoteAttribution.Explain` on the finished live run's own inputs (the party's persuasion by action, the attacks it received, its coverage, the total per party, the setup's compatibility, prior and loyalty), kept past the run's own clearing. ⚠ Until this pass `VoteAttribution.Explain` had been called only by the harness with staged inputs; this is its first live caller. A night with no live campaign says "no live campaign was run to this election".
- **The Docket.** A MINISTER ALERTS card before the decision cards names each portfolio whose minister has something to say - a pending cabinet decision is the one thing the cabinet emits today (P2-5 gives ministers attributes and the region real events) - with the minister's name and philosophy and the decision's name; and under every option's button its cost and impact as the desk says them: the budget figure on the country's own scale (P2-0.1's rule) and the option's shocks as arrows (crime, poverty, approval, trade balance, youth unemployment - the authored figures `ApplyDecisionOption` applies, drawn, not estimated).

**The film:** the sweep (`p2dk1280_*`, `p2dk2560_*`: the Docket `03_decisions`, the signing `89d_signing_entrance` / `89e_signing_settled`) and the interrupts pass (`p2di1280_*`, `p2di2560_*`: election night `e7c` / `e7d`) at both widths.

**Bar:** `RunSimulationBatch` and `RunAllBatch` clean on the committed tree (`bar39_p2_4_3_*.log`).

**What the films taught.** The first pass compiled only at the third launch - the night's `Build` had gained the ledger's call in its body builder before either signature carried the two parameters (the splice's edit missed the wrapped signature line, and the body builder is a second method). The first frames then showed the frame full but the panels stating absence: the harness stages its two divisions straight into the log with the old four-argument `Append`, so they carried no sides and no estimate. The harness now stages them through `RecordDivision` and attaches the standing preview's arrows (`StageDivisionWithContent`, which says in its own log line that the harness holds no draft), so the ceremony on film shows the map and the arrows. The ledger's heading named a region - `CampaignRun.State.Names` are the regions, the party names are the setup's - and was corrected.
